title: Villa for Rent Koh Samui Long Term: Expert Tips for Extended Stays
description: Looking for a villa for rent in Koh Samui long term? Learn how to negotiate rates, choose the right area, and what to expect for stays of 1–6 months.

blocks.text: A villa for rent in Koh Samui long term has become one of the most sought-after arrangements for remote workers, retirees, and extended holiday travellers. With its year-round warm climate, reliable infrastructure, and spectacular scenery, the island lends itself perfectly to longer stays. But long-term villa rental in Koh Samui has its own rules — here’s what you need to know.
What Counts as Long Term in Koh Samui?

Most villa managers define long-term as anything from one month upwards. The sweet spot for the best rates is typically 3–6 months. Some villas offer monthly rates even for 30-day stays, while others require a minimum of two months to unlock significant discounts.

Long-term rates are almost always negotiable in Koh Samui. As a benchmark, expect 30–50% off the peak nightly rate when booking for a full month, and 40–60% off for three months or more. The shoulder season (May–October) offers the most room to negotiate, as occupancy drops and owners prefer a reliable long-stay guest to vacant nights.

One of the island’s most desirable areas for long-term residents. Quiet, residential, and close to excellent amenities — Tops Supermarket, Villa Market, the Big Buddha temple, and Bangrak Pier are all within 5–10 minutes. The sea views from hillside properties here are among the island’s finest.

The Fisherman’s Village area is popular with European expats and long-term visitors. A strong café culture, French and Italian restaurants, and a laid-back pace make it easy to settle in for months. Bangrak Beach is adjacent.

The most affordable of the northern beaches. A long stretch of quiet sand, excellent local food, and a growing expat community make Maenam an underrated choice for long-stay visitors on a tighter budget.
Better suited to short stays. The noise and party culture of Chaweng makes it less comfortable for extended living, though the convenience of its restaurants and services is undeniable.
What to Include in a Long-Term Rental Contract

items: Utility caps — confirm who pays for electricity and water. Electricity in Thailand is priced at commercial rates for tourist accommodation, so air conditioning costs can add significantly to your monthly bill.
Maintenance responsibilities — pool cleaning, garden, pest control. Who arranges and pays?
WiFi speed guarantee — ask for a written commitment on minimum speeds if you work remotely.
Housekeeping frequency — daily, weekly, or on request? What’s included?
Early termination clause — what’s the penalty if your plans change?

blocks.text: Thai tourist visas are granted for 30 days on arrival (extendable once at the Koh Samui immigration office for a further 30 days). For stays beyond 60 days, you’ll need a tourist visa obtained from a Thai consulate before arriving, or to make a border run. The TR visa gives 60 days plus one extension of 30 days — a total of 90 days in-country. Longer-term options include the Thailand Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa introduced in 2022, available to remote workers earning above a certain income threshold.
Day-to-Day Living on a Long-Term Koh Samui Stay

After the first week, the island settles into a comfortable rhythm. Morning markets in Maenam and Bangrak run from around 6–9 am and sell fresh fruit, vegetables, and local food at excellent prices. The big shopping centres (Central Festival, Makro) are in the Chaweng area. Healthcare is provided by Bangkok Hospital Samui and Samui International Hospital — both offer expatriate services and English-speaking staff.
